# About DataFinder

<span id="f389b24b"></span>
## SaaS\-cloud\-native

With the development of DataFinder products, there are currently two categories of product environments in the BytePlus SaaS environment: SaaS\-cloud\-native environments (new SaaS environments).


* The two types of environments have **inconsistent reporting addresses when accessing event tracking**, and **inconsistent management operations such as administrators' projects/applications**.

* The operation process of other data analytics, data governance, Dashboard and other functions is basically the same.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">Before you do the operation, you need to understand what kind of environment your current environment is, and check the corresponding help document according to the environment:</div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">How can I confirm whether my SaaS environment is a SaaS\-cloud native environment? See <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/SaaS_Cloud-Native_Privatized_Environments">SaaS Cloud\-Native & Privatized Environments</a>.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">What are the event tracking data reporting addresses for different environments? See <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Data_Reporting_Address">Data Reporting Address</a>.</div>



<span id="be2183d9"></span>
## Value\-added features/whitelist features

DataFinder provides you with rich data Transmission Service, analysis, governance and other functions.


* Some functions are value\-added functions that you need to purchase separately to use, such as advertising monitoring, virtual projects, multi\-ID criteria, Bitable, etc.

* We will also continue to release new features, some of which may only be available to whitelisted users.


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">If you do not find the feature shown in the document in your current environment, possibly because the feature is a value\-added feature or is only available to whitelisted users, you can refer to the purchase guide in the document, the whitelisted application guide to make a purchase, or apply for whitelisting.</div>

# About the fee

<span id="1a40b170"></span>
## Billing event volume statistics criteria

When you open the purchase of DataFinder, you will choose the corresponding usage statistics criteria ( **effective event volume** or **MTU** ) when signing the contract.


|Dosage criteria description |Valid event |MTU |
|---|---|---|
|Calculation method |The sum of all valid events reported is counted. |According to the SSID criteria, users who have had valid events in the past month are counted.<br><br>Valid events include the following three categories:<br><br><br>* Pre\-set events, details can refer to: [Preset Property Summary Table](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Preset_Property_Summary_Table).<br><br>* User\-defined code event tracking events.<br><br>* Events automatically reported after the SDK function is enabled include:<br><br>   * Full event tracking<br><br>   * The web page automatically collects the page dwell time |
|Calculation timing |The statistics of the previous day will be completed at 10:00 the next day. |The statistics for the previous month will be completed at 10:00 on the 1st of each month. |

* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">If an event is disabled in data management, the corresponding event will not be reported and will not be counted in event usage. To disable event actions, see: <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/General_Events#735cf495">Enable/disable/hide events</a>.</div>



<span id="0f08b757"></span>
## Data storage/valid period

After the data is reported to the DataFinder, the DataFinder will save it for you for a certain period of time. **After the storage valid period is exceeded, the historical data will be lost**.


* See the storage valid period each environment offers you: [Product Usage Restrictions](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Product_Usage_Restrictions).


<span id="fab53b6d"></span>
## Check the usage

You can view the current usage on the Group Settings page of the DataFinder console. For the operation entry, see: [Check product usage](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Product_Usage_Standard_and_Statistics#c0eced57).

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>

<span id="ff7da89c"></span>
# About permission control

<span id="f4fa77b7"></span>
## authority control ability

The permission control of DataFinder is mainly based on the RBAC permission control strategy, that is, the core control idea is to add specific users as role members by planning the permission scope of different roles, so as to realize the detailed permission control of users. The granularity of control includes: group level, project level, application level, DataFinder function level, DataFinder data and data desensitization level, Dashboard/chart level, details:


* SaaS\-cloud native: [Permission Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Permission_Management), [Dashboard Permission Description](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Dashboard_Permission_Description)


<span id="3c2ce341"></span>
# Calculation method

<span id="71fa7305"></span>
## Group, project, application

DataFinder's product resource management can be carried out from the group, project, and application dimensions. It is recommended that you use DataFinder to plan assets according to your own business classification and personnel organization.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />


* Group: A group is a team space, and the group name is usually the company name or account name filled in when registering a BytePlus account. In the group, you can create projects, create applications, and conduct data analytics.

* Projects: Projects can be used to isolate applications, user roles, etc. under the group.

* Application: refers to a product that belongs to the user (or the user's team) and needs to be monitored for changes and fluctuations in data.


<span id="cb24d415"></span>
## Analytical Agents & multi\-Agents

The actual business analysis process needs to clarify the core object or focus of the analysis, usually the "subject" refers to the users who use the product or service. However, in some scenarios, it may also be necessary to analyze multiple subjects, such as the automotive industry, which needs to carry out data analytics from different perspectives such as consumers, automobiles, and merchants.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>

<span id="e402fdc3"></span>
## Statistical criteria & unique user identification

Usually, when we use advanced analysis for data analytics, the growth analysis (DataFinder) will default to the **user** as the object of statistical analysis, and use the SSID as the user's unique identification ID to calculate the indicator. When your analysis object is a user, it is recommended to keep the default statistical criteria ssid. DataFinder can restore a real user individual through an ssid after mapping the user's device_id/web_id, user_unique_id, etc. by ID_Mapping. See [User ID (uid, ssid, did)](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/User_ID_uid_ssid_did)[ ](https://www.volcengine.com/docs/84129/1261513)for details.

In addition, growth analysis also provides the ability to switch statistical criteria to meet the scenario of counting user behavior data according to criteria other than the user SSID, and then performing user analysis. Operational instructions for creating and using other statistical criteria: [Statistical Criteria](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Statistical_Criteria).

<span id="8c32aad7"></span>
## User ID & Multi\-ID Types

DataFinder supports device_id/web_id/anonymous_id, user_unique_id, ssid to identify users/devices.


* device_id, web_id, anonymous_id: can be used as the unique id of the device, mostly in scenarios where the user's real\-name id cannot be obtained.

* user_unique_id: for the login state user identity, mostly in the user can get the real name ID use of the scene, the general situation directly using the product business user identity, such as login account. When the user_unique_id is not set, in the SaaS version, the system will automatically use device_id/web_id instead.

* SSID: for the DataFinder user statistics criteria ID, with the device identification device_id/web_id, login state user identification user_unique_id mutual Mapping, can ensure the user anonymity and ID unity in the real name state.


A simple schematic diagram of the mapping of the three types of IDs is as follows. For more information on user IDs, please refer to [User ID (uid, ssid, did)](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/User_ID_uid_ssid_did).

# Event tracking design event tracking scheme

<span id="953486b0"></span>
## Supported event tracking types: code event tracking (used in conjunction with preset events/properties), full event tracking


|Comparison term |Code event tracking |Full event tracking |
|---|---|---|
|Event tracking |Code event tracking refers to the development engineer, according to business personalized needs, manually write the code to achieve data collection logic. |Full event tracking, also known as "no event tracking", "no trace event tracking" and "automatic event tracking". Full event tracking is automatically collected and reported for the browsing of criteria pages and the clicking of criteria elements, without the need to develop and develop code for event tracking integration. |
|Capture event |The acquisition range is wide, and theoretically, as long as it is an interactive operation on the application side, it can be collected.<br><br><br>* DataFinder provides you with preset events and properties that you can combine with the supported preset events and properties to supplement with custom code event tracking.<br><br>* For details of supported preset events/properties, see: [Preset Property Summary Table](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Preset_Property_Summary_Table). |All event tracking events collected are bav2b_click button clicks, bav2b_page page browsing and other events. For details, see [Full Event Tracking Preset Events and Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Full_Event_Tracking_Preset_Events_and_Properties). |
|Applicable scenario |* It is suitable for scenarios where the logic of related fields of the collection and analysis business is tight, and the analysis is more focused.<br><br>* Especially some non\-click, **non\-visual** behavior, non\-code event tracking implementation is not possible<br><br><br>For example: search results return, registration results return, banner, floor, personalized recommendation/thousand people and thousands of faces page |* Applicable to activity pages, landing pages, simple analysis of UV, PV, clicks and other basic indicators;<br><br>* Simple analysis or statistical requirements, events that do not require custom attribute settings such as parameter transfer for event tracking events; |
|Advantage |* Complete business information;<br><br>* Events, properties, reporting timing, etc. can be customized and controlled<br><br>* Capable of fully restoring user behavior links |* No need for developers to enter manually, the least intrusive to business code,  **++less work ++** ;<br><br>* Full event tracking event data is automatically and continuously collected when the SDK is deployed, which means that even if specific events are not explicitly specified to analyze initially, full event tracking's continuous and comprehensive data collection enables **data re\-run** \- that is, past data can be queried and analyzed at any time. |
|Disadvantage |* The event tracking of each control needs to add corresponding code, which is a lot of work and requires developer support and coupling with business code;<br><br>* After the version is launched, the iteration flexibility of event tracking content is low |* Undifferentiated full collection generates invalid data reporting, wasting traffic/storage/computing resources;<br><br>* Unable to collect business\-related properties, automatic collection of all event data, automatic collection of all event data<br><br>* There are some limitations to the development framework, as detailed in the full event tracking section of the [Client side](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/SDK_Feature_List#%E5%AE%A2%E6%88%B7%E7%AB%AF) SDK support scope.<br><br>* If you need to target specific user behavior, you need to combine virtual events or circled event functions to achieve |
|Integrated Operations Guide |* Preset events and properties: You don't need to do any configuration, and the corresponding data will be automatically collected and reported according to the triggering mechanism.<br><br>* Custom code event tracking:<br><br>   * First, according to the business analysis needs, plan the custom event tracking and attributes that need to be collected and reported.<br><br>   * Enter the corresponding event tracking and properties in the DataFinder console, and drop the event tracking and property names into the library first.<br><br>   * When integrating the SDK, refer to the operation guide for reporting code event tracking to configure. |* When integrating the SDK, turn on the full event tracking switch. |
|Stop data reporting |If you don't want to collect and report some code event tracking data, you can disable the corresponding event or attribute in the **Data Management** \> **metadata management** of the DataFinder console. |If you do not want to collect and report full event tracking data, you can turn off the full event tracking switch in the DataFinder console project center \> project management \> SDK settings. No need to modify the full event tracking switch in the integration code. |
|Data analysis |* Heat map and circle event functions can only be used if full event tracking is enabled. ||

# Data access and reporting

<span id="0bfd27f2"></span>
## Precautions for data reporting


* Enter before reporting: If you need to report custom event tracking data, you need to create corresponding events and properties on the DataFinder's Data Management \> Metadata Management page first, and enter the custom event tracking data into the DataFinder first, and then the subsequent custom event tracking data can be reported normally. See [General Events](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/General_Events).

* Confirm the reporting address before reporting: What is the event tracking data reporting address for different environments? See [Data Reporting Address](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Data_Reporting_Address).

* Data quantity limit: When reporting data, you first check the current data quantity limit. If the number limit is exceeded, the excess event and attribute data may be automatically discarded by the system. The total number of events reported by a single application, the types of meta events supported by a single application, the number of attributes of a single event, the number of attributes of user attributes, and the limit of the number of public attributes of a single application custom event, see: [3. Restrictions on reporting data](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification#_3-%E4%B8%8A%E6%8A%A5%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E9%99%90%E5%88%B6).

## Data reporting address

When reporting data access, you need to confirm your data reporting address according to the current environment type and terminal type. If the reporting address is set incorrectly, you will not be able to check the reported data later: [Data Reporting Address](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Data_Reporting_Address).

<span id="2ea447db"></span>
## Preset events/properties, custom events/properties

DataFinder provides you with a wealth of commonly used preset events and properties. You can start by looking at the currently supported preset events and properties: [Preset Property Summary Table](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Preset_Property_Summary_Table). You can also enter custom event tracking into DataFinder according to business needs, and then report custom event tracking data for user behavior analysis.


|**Event/Attribute Classification** ||**Business Meaning Statement** |
|---|---|---|
|System preset |Preset event public properties |General properties that are reported for each event preset by the system. For example, the device information class field reported by the Finder SDK. |
||Preset events and event properties |System preset event tracking events and event properties. |
||Preset user properties |System\-preset properties that describe the user's own state. |
|Custom |Custom event public properties |Customer\-defined event public properties other than the preset event public properties. |
||Custom events and event properties |Customer\-defined events and event properties other than preset events and event properties. |
||Custom user properties |Customer\-defined user properties other than the preset user properties. |

## Report result verification


* During the development of the Data Transmission Service SDK, you can first check the error\-prone configuration of the integrated SDK at each end; then verify it during the integration process, such as using the real\-time event tracking monitoring function provided by DataFinder and using Devtools tools for verification.

* Integrated SDK development is completed, the data began to report: after the data access SDK development is completed, you can take the initiative to construct some event tracking data for reporting verification, **usually wait 10 to 15 minutes later ** can be in DataFinder's metadata management page to view data reporting records, use analysis tools to query the reported data.


For more information on event tracking validation, see the [General Event Tracking Verification Operation Guide](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/General_Event_Tracking_Verification_Operation_Guide).

# Analytical metrics


* You can create common analytical indicators as solidified indicators in a unified page, so that you can directly choose to use them in multiple analytical tools: [Metrics Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Metrics_Management).

* You can combine multiple general events in the DataFinder into virtual events through certain logical relationships, and then perform user behavior analysis through virtual events: [Virtual Events](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Virtual_Events).

   For example, I want to see the number of deduplicate users for which event A or event B occurred. For example, the number of deduplicated users who viewed page A or page B. At this point, a virtual event is required: it indicates that either event A or event B occurs.


<span id="03358365"></span>
# Data dashboard

<span id="2d4a88d2"></span>
## Dashboard construction and authority control


* If you have "Public Space Management Permissions", you can create Dashboard boards in public or personal spaces.

* If you don't have "public space management permission", you can only create and add Dashboard boards to your personal space.

* Dashboard board created into public space: After creation, it is visible to all members by default, and you can modify the viewing scope through the "Share" function.

* Dashboard created into a private space: After creation, it is only visible to yourself by default. You can share the Dashboard with others for viewing (corresponding to viewing permissions) or collaborative editing (corresponding to editing permissions) through the "Share" function.

* You can share the board with others through the "Share" function (corresponding to viewing permissions) or collaborative editing (corresponding to editing permissions).


<span id="afa67d51"></span>
## Dashboard Subscription/Monitoring


* DataFinder's Dashboard supports picture subscriptions through email/Lark group/DingTalk group, and a single Dashboard can subscribe up to 20 items: [Dashboard Subscription](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Dashboard_Subscription).

* On Dashboard, we can keep an eye on fluctuations in key data by creating monitoring tasks. According to the monitoring rules, it can automatically determine whether the indicator fluctuates within the normal range, and trigger an alarm (email) when abnormal, without manual daily tracking judgment, to achieve automatic monitoring: [Monitoring Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Monitoring_Management).


<span id="1e849191"></span>
## Dashboard inlay

Dashboard and chart embedding refers to embedding DataFinder's Dashboard boards/charts into external platforms, such as reporting platforms, Lark documents, or your company's own business systems. Through this ability, you will get a link belonging to the Dashboard/chart. For users with the Dashboard/chart permission account, they can directly view the embedded Dashboard/chart on the external platform through this link: [1.2.1 Dashboard embedding](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Dashboard_Openness#_1-2-1-%E7%9C%8B%E6%9D%BF%E5%B5%8C%E5%87%BA).

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">Dashboard embedded in this way requires the current account to be logged in. When not logged in, you need to log in to BytePlus first, and then open the Dashboard embedded page.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">When using custom permissions, no account is required to be logged in. If the embedded environment requires custom permissions, please check < <a href="https://bytedance.feishu.cn/docx/S2j3dCy6KoA2VXx19WrcZm9Nn5e">DataFinder Dashboard Analysis Integration Solution </a>\> first.</div>
